Let the centre of the semicircle be the origin and put  

\[
A=(-8,0),\qquad B=(8,0),\qquad \omega:\;x^{2}+y^{2}=8^{2},\;y\ge 0 .
\]

Take a variable point \(P\) on the diameter \(AB\); write  

\[
P=(p,0)\qquad (-8\le p\le 8).
\]

---

### 1.  The points \(Q,M,C,D\)

The point of the semicircle whose projection on \(AB\) is \(P\) is  

\[
Q=\bigl(p,\sqrt{64-p^{2}}\bigr).
\]

The midpoint of \(PQ\) is  

\[
M=\Bigl(p,\frac{\sqrt{64-p^{2}}}{2}\Bigr)\qquad\bigl(y_{0}:=\frac{\sqrt{64-p^{2}}}{2}\bigr).
\]

The line through \(M\) perpendicular to \(PQ\) is the horizontal line  

\[
y=y_{0}.
\]

Intersecting this line with the circle gives  

\[
x^{2}+y_{0}^{2}=64\Longrightarrow 
x^{2}=64-y_{0}^{2}=48+\frac{p^{2}}{4}.
\]

Hence  

\[
C=\Bigl(-\sqrt{48+\frac{p^{2}}{4}},\,y_{0}\Bigr),\qquad 
D=\Bigl(\;\sqrt{48+\frac{p^{2}}{4}},\,y_{0}\Bigr).
\]

---

### 2.  Areas of the two quadrilaterals  

The quadrilateral \(PMCA\) can be split by the diagonal \(PC\) into

* \(\triangle PMC\) – a right triangle with legs \(PM=y_{0}\) and \(MC=p-x_{C}\);
* \(\triangle PCA\) – its base \(PA=p+8\) lies on the \(x\)-axis, so its altitude is also \(y_{0}\).

Thus  

\[
\begin{aligned}
[PMCA]&=\frac12\,y_{0}(p-x_{C})+\frac12\,y_{0}(p+8)\\[2mm]
      &=\frac12\,y_{0}\bigl(2p-x_{C}+8\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]

In the same way  

\[
\begin{aligned}
[PMDB]&=\frac12\,y_{0}(x_{D}-p)+\frac12\,y_{0}(8-p)\\[2mm]
      &=\frac12\,y_{0}\bigl(x_{D}+8-2p\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### 3.  The difference of the areas  

\[
\begin{aligned}
[PMCA]-[PMDB]
  &=\frac12\,y_{0}\Bigl[2p-x_{C}+8-(x_{D}+8-2p)\Bigr]\\[2mm]
  &=\frac12\,y_{0}\Bigl[4p-(x_{D}+x_{C})\Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]

Because \(x_{D}+x_{C}=0\), we obtain the very simple formula  

\[
[PMCA]-[PMDB]=2p\,y_{0}=p\sqrt{64-p^{2}}\qquad (p\ge 0).
\]

For \(p<0\) the sign reverses, so the absolute difference is  

\[
\Delta(p)=|p|\sqrt{64-p^{2}},\qquad -8\le p\le 8.
\]

---

### 4.  Maximising the difference  

Set \(p\ge0\) (the problem is symmetric).  
Define  

\[
f(p)=p\sqrt{64-p^{2}},\qquad 0\le p\le 8 .
\]

\(f^{2}(p)=p^{2}(64-p^{2})=64p^{2}-p^{4}\) is a quadratic in \(p^{2}\); it attains its maximum when  

\[
p^{2}= \frac{64}{2}=32\quad\Longrightarrow\quad p=4\sqrt2 .
\]

Then  

\[
f_{\max}=p\sqrt{64-p^{2}}=4\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt{64-32}=4\sqrt2\cdot4\sqrt2=32 .
\]

Thus the largest possible value of the difference of the two areas is  

\[
\boxed{32}.
